inputs.source: On call engineer chat request (SSO authenticated)

instructions.note: The prompt authorizes production deploys and migrations on request and explicitly instructs the agent not to ask for confirmation.

controls.name: Only on call engineers can access the assistant
controls.decay_rationale: Access restriction does not decay with model capability, but it does not restore attributable provenance for actions taken with the engineer's delegated token.

controls.name: Cloud audit logging of production actions
controls.decay_rationale: Logging does not decay with model capability, but the record attributes actions only to the engineer identity and not distinctly to the agent.

controls.name: Tamper-resistant per-action provenance linking engineer request, agent decision, and production action
controls.decay_rationale: A separate immutable action record enforced outside the model would not decay with model capability and would restore attributable provenance.

controls.name: Immutable retention for action-justifying chat records
controls.decay_rationale: Retention enforced at the store would preserve the only request-and-rationale record against later user deletion and would not decay with model capability.

findings.title: Shared engineer identity and deletable chat history leave production actions non-attributable

evidence.observation: The agent uses the on call engineer's personal access token passed in at session start, so production actions are executed under the engineer's identity rather than a distinct agent identity.

Every production action is recorded in the cloud audit log under the engineer's name, so the audit record does not distinguish which actions were directly performed by the engineer versus by the agent.
The only record of what the agent was asked, and why it acted, is the chat transcript, and engineers can delete their own chat history.
Database migrations cannot be rolled back automatically, making the affected capability consequential and partially irreversible.

The prompt directs the agent to deploy services or run migrations in production when asked and says not to ask for confirmation, supporting A3 act-then-report behavior without an attributable approval record.

recommendations.action: Add immutable per-action provenance that binds engineer identity, exact request, agent execution trace, and production action id in a tamper-resistant record distinct from the user's deletable chat history.
Prevent deletion of chat records that justify production actions, or copy the action-relevant subset into an immutable evidence store at execution time.

forecast.watch_signal: Raise reassessment if unattended step counts or runtime increase, or if logging and record-retention settings change; the present design already lacks attributable provenance, so these triggers do not increase the tier further.

stride_coverage.rationale: The provided artifacts describe no self-configuration path, tool-definition updates, or writable prompt/configuration surface for this agent design.
The design contains no read or egress capability that discloses data outside the trust boundary; it only performs production actions for authenticated engineers.
The artifacts describe two bounded production actions and no looping, spending, recursive delegation, or long-running unattended execution behavior.
The artifacts do not say whether integrity protection or change controls exist on the production deploy invocation path.
This boundary-crossing flow performs a production deployment action and is not described as carrying confidential payloads outside the organization.
No evidence shows repeated or unbounded deploy invocation over this flow; the design exposes a single bounded administrative action.
The artifacts do not say whether integrity protection or change controls exist on the database migration invocation path.
This boundary-crossing flow invokes a migration and is not described as disclosing sensitive data outside the trust boundary.
The design describes a single production migration action, not an unbounded or volumetric traffic pattern over this flow.
The artifacts do not state retention access controls, tenant separation, or transcript confidentiality protections for chat history.
The risk evidenced here is deletable provenance, not loss of service availability, and no quota or saturation issue is described for the transcript store.
The artifacts do not state whether the cloud audit log is immutable or protected from alteration by privileged insiders.
The artifacts do not state who can read cloud audit logs or whether logs expose sensitive operational details.
No evidence indicates quota exhaustion or unavailability of the audit log store; the present issue is attribution quality rather than service loss.

rating.rationale: Present risk is dominated by a property finding: consequential production actions are executed with the engineer's delegated identity, the cloud audit log attributes them only to that engineer, and the only request-and-rationale record is deletable chat history. No declared control restores attributable provenance, so residual stays at the section 5a inherent level. Forecast remains high because the core deficiency already exists today; increasing autonomy or task horizon would warrant reassessment but does not raise the tier above the present high.

limitations: This assessment reflects the declared design and configuration in the provided prompt and runtime notes, not observed runtime behavior or verified enforcement.
No source code, IaC, or runtime configuration was provided, so integrity protections, exact deploy and migration tool semantics, and audit log immutability could not be verified.
Manual validation was applied against the provided schema and validation checklist because scripts could not be run in this environment.
